title: Second order N-Electron Valence state Perturbation Theory for polaritonic systems
abstract: Molecules strongly coupled to optical cavities often show multi-configurational character, which the cavity can enhance by mixing electronic states. Describing them accurately requires a complete treatment of correlation between all the involved quantum particles. The available QED ab-initio methods do not treat it in its completeness except for QED-FCI. We extend second-order N-electron valence state perturbation theory (NEVPT2) to polaritonic chemistry, in its state-specific (QED-NEVPT2) and quasi degenerate (QED-QD-NEVPT2) forms. Here, the correlation due to the interaction of more degenerate configurations comes from a QED-CASSCF reference, while that associated with instantaneous interactions between the particles is added by second-order perturbation theory. Application of the methods to ammonia, ethylene and formaldimine revealed that this approach represents the perfect alternative to the well established QED-Coupled Cluster approach when the molecular system is described by more degenerate configurations. The approaches developed in this work have the potential to become state-of-the-art methodologies for the description of reactivity and photochemistry in polaritonic systems.

summaries.en: This work extends second-order N-electron valence state perturbation theory to polaritonic systems in state-specific (QED-NEVPT2) and quasi-degenerate (QED-QD-NEVPT2) forms, using a QED-CASSCF reference to capture strong correlation among degenerate configurations while adding instantaneous particle interactions perturbatively, and applications to ammonia, ethylene, and formaldimine show it is a strong alternative to QED-Coupled Cluster for multiconfigurational molecular systems.

title: High-speed laser speckle contrast imaging of the human retina
abstract: We demonstrate real-time laser speckle contrast imaging of the human retina using a Phantom S980 streaming camera at $3840\times2160$ pixels, 8-bit depth, and 1000 frames per second, with a $988\,\mu\mathrm{s}$ exposure. We report four recordings of the peripapillary retina around the optic disc in the right eye of one healthy 25-year-old emmetropic man, acquired without pharmacological pupil dilation, using 852-nm diffuse Maxwellian illumination at an entering optical power of 5.0 mW. Each recording contained 4096 frames (4.10 s), and all 16384 frames in the reported recordings were retained. Open-source Holoflow software on an NVIDIA RTX 5090 computes $K=\sigma/\mu$ over $5\times5$ spatial pixels and nonoverlapping blocks of 16 frames, producing 62.5 contrast maps/s with 60-frame/s rendering and no additional averaging. The nominal raw-input throughput is 8.29 Gpixel/s. Main retinal arterial and venous branches and smaller peripapillary vessels were visualized. Variations during the cardiac cycle were visible in the principal retinal arteries and veins, as illustrated in the Supplementary Videos. Regional inverse-contrast traces show an arterial dicrotic notch and spontaneous venous pulsation. This single-volunteer demonstration establishes an operating point for high-throughput retinal speckle-contrast visualization. Physiological observations are descriptive; contrast is an instrument-dependent observable rather than a calibrated blood-flow velocity.

title: Electro-optic comb-driven massive data transmission on monolithically integrated lithium niobate photonic circuits
abstract: Driven by large AI models, the demand for datacenter interconnects is outstripping traditional scaling laws. This necessitates a transition toward dense multiplexing techniques, such as wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM), for datacenter environments, transferring long-haul spectral efficiency to short-reach, high-bandwidth applications. Integrated optical frequency combs offer compact, low-cost light sources for future datacenter WDM interconnects. However, existing Kerr comb and mode-locked laser implementations suffer from drawbacks in power efficiency, spectral flatness and phase noise. Their fixed, device-specific channel spacings often conflict with standard WDM grids, and co-integration with high-speed modulators remains challenging. Here, we overcome these limitations by demonstrating high-capacity data transmission using flat-top electro-optic combs on thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN), a platform featuring flat spectra, tunable wavelengths and comb spacing, alongside native compatibility with (de-)multiplexers and high-speed modulators. Using 46 wavelength channels from two lasers and a 50-GHz on-chip electro-optic comb, we realize 16.56 Tb/s coherent transmission over a 98.84-km deployed fiber link between two universities and two datacenters in Hong Kong, verifying its suitability for inter-datacenter connections. To highlight grid reconfigurability, we reconfigure the comb to 100-GHz spacing via an on-chip demultiplexer and demonstrate 10-channel, 80-GBaud coherent transmission at 6.4 Tb/s. We further report a proof-of-concept monolithic WDM transmitter integrating the comb and high-speed modulator, achieving 19-channel, 45-GBaud IM/DD transmission at 1.71 Tb/s. Our work validates TFLN electro-optic combs as flexible, compact and scalable WDM engines for both coherent and IM/DD datacenter links to satisfy rapidly rising bandwidth requirements.

title: Why Emission Spectral Profile of Diverse Fluoro-phores Look Alike with Thick Polymer Overlayers?
abstract: Fluorescence from fluorophore-polymer overlayers reflects an interplay between molecular photo-physics and thickness dependent optical propagation. Combining spectrally resolved single mole-cule measurements, transition dipole moment orientation analysis and ensemble fluorescence, we show that structurally and photophysically distinct fluorophores can exhibit similar red shifted emission profiles under thick polymer overlayers even without additional reflecting surface. This similarity indicates a common optical transfer function imposed by the overlayer rather than a pure-ly fluorophore specific molecular response. Although local molecular interactions, excited state dy-namics and vibronic coupling govern intrinsic emission, the overlayer modifies detected spectra through refractive index contrast, dielectric boundary reflections, cavity effects and collection ge-ometry. Vibronic energy spacing distributions remain largely preserved as thickness changes, whereas spectral positions and relative intensities vary systematically. Thus, polymer thickness pri-marily reshapes detected spectrum through optical propagation and outcoupling while retaining vi-brational modes. Time dependent density functional theory identifies candidate Franck-Condon and Herzberg-Teller active dye modes contributing to spectral fluctuations and dipole reorientation.

summaries.en: Thick polymer overlayers produce similar red-shifted emission profiles across structurally and photophysically distinct fluorophores because a common optical transfer function—arising from refractive index contrast, dielectric boundary reflections, cavity effects and collection geometry—reshapes the detected spectra via optical propagation and outcoupling while largely preserving vibronic energy spacings.

title: Toward Integrated Microwave Diagnostics for Future Fusion Devices: Design of a Compact Waveguide Diplexer
abstract: Microwave diagnostics are essential for plasma control and physics studies in magnetic confinement fusion, providing measurements of electron density, electron temperature, and energetic-particle behavior. However, diagnostic access in future burning-plasma reactors will be severely constrained by breeding blankets, neutron shielding, and compact reactor geometries, requiring reduced blanket opening areas while maintaining diagnostic capability. This work presents a compact waveguide diplexer for front-end integration of multiple microwave diagnostics. The proposed diplexer combines a waveguide T-junction with two iris-coupled sixth-order Chebyshev bandpass filters, enabling microwave reflectometry and electron cyclotron emission (ECE) diagnostics to share a common transmission line while operating in separate frequency bands. As an initial study, the diplexer is designed for the 65-70 GHz reflectometry and 85-90 GHz ECE systems on the J-TEXT tokamak. Full-wave electromagnetic simulations demonstrate insertion losses below 1 dB and channel isolation exceeding 40 dB across both operating bands. The proposed methodology provides a compact and scalable approach to microwave diagnostic integration and establishes a practical basis for multi-diagnostic front-end systems in future fusion devices.

summaries.en: This work presents a compact waveguide diplexer that combines a T-junction with two iris-coupled sixth-order Chebyshev bandpass filters to let 65-70 GHz reflectometry and 85-90 GHz ECE diagnostics share a common transmission line, with full-wave simulations showing insertion loss below 1 dB and channel isolation above 40 dB.

title: Data-efficient linear hyperspectral imaging through risk-guided co-design
abstract: Computational hyperspectral imaging reconstructs spatial-spectral information from limited optical measurements. Linear reconstructors are efficient and interpretable, but often underperform deep nonlinear models, which typically require substantial training data and computational resources. Here we present a theory-guided encoding-reconstruction co-design framework that achieves, to our knowledge, state-of-the-art linear reconstruction performance. We establish a theory for the exact five-term decomposition of reconstruction risk and introduce a method for diagnosing the statistical-coverage lower bound within a fixed principal component analysis envelope, which together inform the optimized design of hyperspectral imaging systems. The framework applies across coded-aperture snapshot spectral imaging (CASSI), diffractive optical element imaging and spectral filter array imaging, achieving 34.76 dB mean PSNR in single-shot CASSI, outperforming a deep baseline by 9.43 dB with only five source scenes, and matching empirical cross-domain risk within 0.2%. Our results establish a data-efficient and theoretically grounded route to high-performance linear hyperspectral reconstruction, while providing a quantitative basis for identifying whether reconstruction is limited by optical encoding, reconstruction design or statistical coverage.

summaries.en: A theory-guided encoding-reconstruction co-design framework based on an exact five-term decomposition of reconstruction risk and a diagnostic for the statistical-coverage lower bound within a fixed PCA envelope achieves state-of-the-art linear hyperspectral reconstruction, reaching 34.

title: Preparing State-Selected Molecular Beams with high Efficiency using Quantum Cascade Lasers
abstract: We demonstrate the ro-vibrational state-selective preparation of CO molecules ($v$ = 0, J = 0 $\rightarrow$ $v$ = 1, J = 1) in an internally cold molecular beam using a continuous-wave, narrow-linewidth distributed feedback type quantum cascade laser, with an output wavelength of 4.65 $\mu$m. Using a modulation-free wavelength stabilization scheme, we show that population transfer to near saturation levels can be obtained with sufficient long term stability, as needed for state-resolved scattering experiments. We show preliminary results of CO molecules prepared in the $v$ = 1 state, scattering from a clean Cu(100) surface. This study showcases the promise of QCL based excitation for state-selected molecular beam based scattering experiments, especially involving transitions in the mid-infrared domain ($\lambda$ > 4.5 $\mu$m) which are otherwise difficult to access using conventional sources.

title: State-specific perturbation theory for configuration interaction singles: Theoretical analysis, benchmarks, and improvement with size-intensive level shifts
abstract: We recently proposed a state-specific second-order perturbation theory based on the configuration interaction singles (CIS) state, termed CIS(2). Here, we clarify its theoretical connections, assess the accuracy of its excitation energies in greater detail, and develop size-intensive level shifts to improve both accuracy and convergence of its amplitude equations. We first derive the MP2 structure of its working equations and show that our previously introduced Hybrid partition recovers CIS(D) when the ground-state Fock operator is used and the residual Fock action on the CIS reference is neglected. For this partition, an expanded benchmark shows that using the CIS-state Fock operator improves Rydberg and especially charge-transfer accuracy relative to CIS(D), while slightly worsening valence accuracy. We analyze how the hole and particle densities contribute to these changes in excitation energy, which differ among the classes. We then introduce size-intensive level shifts that preserve the ground-state correlation contribution of noninteracting fragments while leaving the ground-state MP2 energy unchanged. With appropriately calibrated parameters, these shifts improve overall accuracy and substantially accelerate convergence without increasing the formal scaling of the amplitude solve. Different optimal parameters for valence and Rydberg states reveal the limitations of a common parameter. The analysis further shows that shifting the contracted-triples block contributes markedly to the excitation-energy correction in addition to accelerating convergence.

summaries.en: This paper clarifies the theoretical connections of the CIS(2) state-specific perturbation theory, benchmarks its excitation energies across valence, Rydberg, and charge-transfer states, and introduces size-intensive level shifts that improve accuracy and substantially accelerate convergence without changing the formal scaling of the amplitude solve.

title: Effects of Pulse Duration on Kerr Self-Focusing and Weld Formation in Ultrafast Laser Welding of Fused Silica
abstract: Kerr self-focusing can shift the laser interaction region away from the geometrical focus, making energy deposition near the joining interface difficult to control. Here, the effect of pulse duration on nonlinear focusing and weld formation is investigated from 262 fs to 10 ps. ICCD imaging shows clear changes in the axial position and shape of the plasma emission. Different pulse durations already produce distinct axial positions during the initial 2000 pulses, and these positions continue to evolve with pulse accumulation. The final weld morphology, weld position, and shear strength show corresponding changes. A ray-optics model including the Kerr effect is used to calculate the focal shift. The simulated trend agrees with the experiment and supports the role of Kerr self-focusing in the observed focal position change. These results clarify the relationship between pulse duration, nonlinear focusing, interaction position, and weld formation.

summaries.en: In ultrafast laser welding of fused silica, increasing pulse duration from 262 fs to 10 ps changes Kerr self-focusing and the axial plasma position, which in turn alters weld morphology, weld position, and shear strength, with a Kerr-effect ray-optics model reproducing the observed focal-shift trend.

title: Rydberg atomic field-enhanced feed beyond electrically small antennas
abstract: The reception of electromagnetic signals becomes increasingly challenging at longer wavelengths, as conventional antenna feeds must scale with the operating wavelength, making it difficult to reconcile compactness with high sensitivity. Rydberg atoms enable direct field-to-optical conversion within deeply subwavelength sensing volumes, yet an effective receiving feed that couples incident fields into the atomic interaction volume remains underdeveloped. Here, we introduce a Rydberg atomic field-enhanced feed (RAFEF) that integrates electromagnetic field capture and enhancement with Rydberg-atomic transduction. We establish a physical model to quantify its receiving capability, Phi, that jointly accounts for sensitivity enhancement, receiving bandwidth and normalized three-dimensional volume, and experimentally obtain Phi_dB = 70.81 dB. Compared with a conventional loop-antenna feed, the RAFEF provides a higher received SNR and overall receiving capability, while its tunable narrowband response enables frequency selectivity directly at the receiving-feed stage. We further demonstrate selective recovery of a target channel from simultaneously incident signals and reception of a 93.5 MHz FM broadcast after approximately 10 km of over-the-air propagation. These results establish the RAFEF as an atomic receiving-feed architecture that exploits localized electric-field transduction to extend Rydberg-atomic reception beyond conventional electrically small antenna feeds.

title: HarP: a simulation tool for high-order harmonic generation and propagation in gases
abstract: Accurately simulating high-order harmonic generation (HHG) for attosecond science requires connecting the microscopic single-atom quantum dynamics and the macroscopic propagation of intense driving laser fields. HarP is an open-source Python code designed to address this multiscale problem. It solves the wave equations for both the driving laser field and the generated harmonics, using precomputed dipole tables for the nonlinear polarization density. This tabulation enables the direct integration of accurate microscopic models while avoiding costly calculations during the propagation. The methodology builds upon the approach of [L'Huillier et al. (1992) PRA 46, 2778] and has already facilitated multiple studies on phase matching, propagation effects and HHG optimization. This paper presents the underlying physical model, its numerical implementation, and comparison against alternative simulation frameworks.

summaries.en: HarP is an open-source Python simulation tool that couples accurate microscopic single-atom dipole dynamics, stored as precomputed tables, with the macroscopic propagation of the driving laser field and generated harmonics to model high-order harmonic generation in gases.

title: Parameter-Decoupling-Informed Learning for Superresolution: Laboratory Validation and Galaxy Imaging
abstract: We present a parameter-decoupling-informed learning model for estimating subwavelength separations of point sources, without requiring prior knowledge of source properties, control over the sources, or continued access to their light signals. The method builds on our parameter-decoupled quantum superresolution estimation theory, which circumvents the need to estimate nuisance parameters such as partial coherence, brightness imbalance, and relative phase. Our convolutional neural network further accommodates practical imperfections, including background noise, photon loss, and centroid and orientation misalignment. We validate the method using synthetic and experimentally generated images, achieving separation-estimation fidelity above $82\%$ for separations as small as approximately $0.075\sigma$, where $\sigma$ is the Gaussian intensity-PSF standard deviation. This corresponds to an illustrative separation of $\sim13.5$ nm when $\sigma=180$ nm, suggesting potential relevance to length scales addressed by advanced active-source microscopy. Applied to archival Hubble images of NGC~4486B, the model yields nuclear separations of 9.3-13.2~pc, consistent with the previously reported value of 12~pc. Comparisons using the same training and testing images demonstrate substantially higher fidelity than conventional direct data-driven learning in the tested cases. The method's robustness to varying source properties and imaging imperfections supports retrospective astrophysical image analysis and motivates applications in live-cell microscopy and quantum metrology where source control or renewed optical measurements are impractical.

title: Optical Speckle Patterns as Nonlinear Feature Maps for Photonic Machine Learning
abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) has increased the demand for energy-efficient hardware, and optical computing has emerged as a promising alternative to conventional electronic processors owing to its high parallelism and potentially lower power consumption. In this work, we investigate an optical computing architecture based on an integrated photonic circular multipass cell, focusing on its suitability for machine learning and pattern recognition tasks. The properties of the system are evaluated through measures of nonlinearity and cosine similarity, which characterize the system's information-processing capacity and the dimensionality of the generated feature representations. Numerical results demonstrate that the reservoir mirror reflectance, the size of the encoded figure, and the refractive-index contrast between the reservoir and the encoded figure modify the nonlinearity of the system, as verified via pairwise similarity estimates. These results indicate that the features generated by the circular multipass cell can be tailored by adjusting the system parameters, providing a means to control the reservoir transformation of the input data. The resulting representations were applied to classification tasks involving texture images and thyroid collagen images, achieving classification accuracies ranging from 69% to 93%. These findings suggest that photonic computing systems could provide a basis for more energy-efficient machine-learning hardware.

summaries.en: This study shows that an integrated photonic circular multipass cell can generate tunable nonlinear speckle-based feature maps whose nonlinearity depends on reservoir mirror reflectance, encoded figure size, and refractive-index contrast, enabling texture and thyroid collagen image classification with 69–93% accuracy.

title: Transverse detuned loading for modulation bandwidth enhancement in VCSELs
abstract: Directly modulated vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers (VCSELs) are central to short-reach optical interconnects, where modulation bandwidth and power efficiency are critical factors for increasing data transfer capacity. Conventional oxide VCSELs still require power-hungry signal processing to achieve high-speed data transmission above 100 Gb/s. Here we report an experimental implementation of detuned loading in a VCSEL to enhance the modulation bandwidth. The detuned loading is achieved by carrier-induced index variations that reshape an engineered transverse mode so its overlap with spatially selective optical losses decreases with increased carrier density. This produces a negative differential loss reminiscent of that in detuned-loaded DBR lasers lasing on the long-wavelength reflectivity flank. The resulting 850 nm single-mode VCSEL exhibits an enhanced carrier-photon relaxation frequency of 44 GHz, yielding a 3dB electrical modulation bandwidth exceeding 50 GHz. The enhancement persists from 25 °C to 75 °C showing the robustness of the mechanism introduced. The same device supports 106.25 Gb/s NRZ transmission without digital signal processing, transmitter pre-emphasis or receiver equalization. These results establish transverse detuned loading as a robust alternative approach for extending the modulation bandwidth of vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers.

title: A low-volume cold-atom microwave clock with an additively manufactured cavity
abstract: We present the performance of a compact microwave interrogated atomic clock based on laser cooled $^{87}$$\rm{Rb}$ atoms. The clock utilizes a micro-fabricated grating magneto-optical trap (gMOT) to cool and trap atoms, and an additively manufactured microwave cavity for microwave interrogation. We demonstrate a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of $370$ at a 1 Hz bandwidth and mid-term instability of $6.7\times10^{-14}$ at an averaging time of $\tau=3 \times 10^{4}$ s. In addition, a low cost mu-metal foil has been implemented on the vacuum chamber to reduce the quadratic Zeeman shift which was previously limiting stability beyond $\tau = 10$ s.

title: Plasma and light: Shaping High Harmonic Generation in Time-Varying Media
abstract: High harmonic generation in solids is typically described under the assumption of a stationary medium. This assumption is rarely questioned because the electronic properties of most media evolve on timescales much slower than the harmonic emission process itself. However, in strongly driven time-varying transparent conductive oxides the plasma frequency, carrier density, and effective mass can evolve on the same femtosecond timescale as harmonic generation. Under these conditions, harmonic generation and material evolution are no longer independent processes. Within this context, we consider a two-field pumping scheme in which a strong field generates a comb of high-order harmonics across a broad spectral window, while a weaker field simultaneously reshapes its own individual spectral lines. Distinct from geometry-dependent wave-mixing processes, the evolving electron plasma reshapes multiple collinear harmonic channels simultaneously. A fully self-consistent hydrodynamic-Maxwell framework reveals that even- and odd-order harmonics naturally emerge from free- and bound-electron dynamics without the typical need to invoke phenomenological nonlinearities. Our model captures the full spectral evolution on an ultra-broad bandwidth, while experiments performed on ITO confirm the distinct behavior of bulk-driven odd harmonics and interface-driven even harmonics under strong pumping. These results establish time-dependent plasma dynamics as a powerful new tool for broadband hyperspectral shaping of multiple harmonic channels beyond the framework of four-wave-mixing processes. Our findings are of particular relevance to ultrafast science, with potential applications in ultrafast pulse manipulation and the generation and control of tailored multi harmonic waveforms.

summaries.en: A self-consistent hydrodynamic-Maxwell model shows that in strongly driven transparent conductive oxides the femtosecond evolution of the electron plasma reshapes multiple collinear high-harmonic channels simultaneously and naturally produces even- and odd-order harmonics from free- and bound-electron dynamics, as confirmed by ITO experiments.

title: Theoretical description of high-harmonic spectroscopy for uniaxial nematic and isotropic liquid crystals
abstract: Enabled by their controllable optical anisotropy, liquid crystals form a cornerstone of linear optical and display technologies. Bringing the versatile platform into the nonlinear regime, we explore its nonlinear optical anisotropy by high-order harmonic generation spectroscopy. Through a comprehensive study targeting gas, liquid, nematic, and crystalline phases, we present a semi-empirical tight-binding approach that provides insight into the intermolecular character of ultrafast light-driven electron dynamics across soft-matter mesophases. We demonstrate how intermolecular electron hybridization enables spectroscopic access to structural properties, such as the nematic director and order parameter. Outlining such foundational mechanisms opens avenues towards nonlinear liquid crystal devices and ultrafast soft-matter spectroscopies.

title: Daylight-Referenced Efficiency (DRE): A Radiometric Measure of Electric Light Source Efficiency
abstract: Photopic luminous efficacy (lm/W) weights optical power strictly against human eye sensitivity V (lambda), creating a systemic metrological penalty for electric light sources engineered with broad spectral output in the ultraviolet (280-380 nm) or infrared (780-4000 nm) bands. Similarly, metrics evaluating chromaticity, color quality, or melanopic pathways assess photoreceptor responses strictly within the visual band, offering no measure of broad-spectrum physical radiant power conversion. To resolve this limitation, we introduce Daylight-Referenced Efficiency (eta_DRE), a radiometric framework that evaluates how efficiently an electric light source converts electrical power into an optical spectrum matching natural terrestrial daylight across domain Omega = [280 nm, 4000 nm]. The framework factorizes performance into primary physical quantities: domain-restricted Wall-Plug Efficiency (eta_wall [W_optical/W_elec]), measuring unweighted electrical-to-optical conversion, and Daylight Spectral Fidelity (eta_spec [unitless, 0-1]), quantifying geometric shape match to the ASTM G173 AM1.5G solar reference via total variation distance (1 - TVD). Multiplying total optical power by spectral fidelity yields the absolute Daylight-Referenced Output Power (P_dr [W]), establishing a direct physical flux quantity for lighting specification. Dividing by electrical drive power gives the summary metric Daylight-Referenced Efficiency (eta_DRE = eta_wall * eta_spec [W/W_elec]), measuring net reference-conforming radiant output per electrical Watt consumed. The mathematical architecture is reference-agnostic, domain-extensible, and maintains provable lower-bound monotonicity for eta_wall and eta_DRE under spectral truncation. Open-source reference software is provided to facilitate deployment and standardized rating of broad-spectrum light sources.

title: Tapering to Enhance the Performance of Nanowire-Based Fluorescent Biosensors
abstract: High-refractive-index nanowires are of interest for signal enhancement in fluorescence-based biosensing. Here, through electromagnetic modelling, we demonstrate substantial fluorescence signal enhancement by incorporating a tapered section into a cylindrical nanowire and investigate two complementary tapering configurations to address practical implementation challenges. Under near-normal excitation, the excitation enhancement increases approximately linearly with taper length, reaching more than three times that of the corresponding non-tapered nanowire at a taper length of 8000 nm. In a non-imaging signal detection scheme using a low numerical aperture (NA), the proposed tapered nanowire achieves more than three orders of magnitude enhancement in fluorescence signal compared with a planar biosensor. Thus, the tapered nanowire should enable efficient fluorescence detection using compact, low-NA optical configuration. In imaging mode, similarly as for non-tapered nanowires, imaging sharpness beyond conventional microscopy limitations is obtained when imaging from the non-tapered nanowire end, while strongly increased excitation enhancement is simultaneously obtained when exciting from the opposite, tapered end.

summaries.en: Electromagnetic modelling shows that adding a tapered section to a high-refractive-index cylindrical nanowire substantially enhances fluorescence excitation and detection, enabling over three orders of magnitude signal enhancement versus a planar biosensor under low-NA detection and providing sharp imaging beyond conventional microscopy limits when imaged from the non-tapered end.

title: Direct tests of conformal symmetry with Rydberg atoms: assessment and proposals
abstract: We propose a direct test of conformal symmetry using Rydberg-atom arrays. By arranging the atoms on a circle and measuring equal-time two-point correlation functions, the characteristic functional form predicted by conformal field theory can be tested directly. We estimate the number of experimental snapshots required to resolve this behavior with sufficient statistical precision. We further optimize the time-dependent ramp profile of the Rabi frequency~$\Omega$ and detuning~$\Delta$ used to prepare the target critical state adiabatically. The optimized profile achieves higher fidelity over much shorter evolution times than those employed in previous experiments. Taken together, these results suggest that a direct experimental test of conformal symmetry is feasible with current Rydberg-atom technology.

title: When is a bosonic operator a Hamiltonian?
abstract: Hermitian polynomials in the quadrature operators $x$ and $p$ are the basic ingredients of continuous-variable quantum information, and increasingly exotic ones are now routinely engineered in superconducting circuits and trapped ions. However, such a polynomial need not define unique quantum dynamics: it may define exactly one, none, or an infinite family of physically distinct ones. Such obstructions are invisible to algebraic arguments and can compromise finite-dimensional truncations, which may fail to converge or silently converge to the wrong dynamics. We develop a method, implemented as an algorithm, which decides which case occurs, and how large the family is, from the coefficients alone, with no functional-analytic input from the user. For Gaussian operators the answer is always one; for non-Gaussian ones, a regime continuous-variable quantum computing cannot do without, the other outcomes occur already for simple and physically natural Hamiltonians. We apply the algorithm to operators drawn from the recent literature.

summaries.en: A new coefficient-based algorithm determines whether a Hermitian polynomial in the quadrature operators x and p defines exactly one, none, or infinitely many physically distinct quantum Hamiltonians, exposing obstructions that algebraic arguments miss and that can cause finite-dimensional truncations to fail or converge silently to wrong dynamics, with nontrivial outcomes arising already for simple non-Gaussian Hamiltonians.
summaries.zh: 一种基于系数的新算法能够判定正交算符x和p的厄米多项式究竟定义唯一、不存在还是无穷多个物理上不同的量子哈密顿量，从而揭示代数论证无法察觉、并可能导致有限维截断失效或悄然收敛到错误动力学的阻碍，而简单的非高斯哈密顿量就已出现非平凡结果。
summaries.ja: 直交演算子xとpのエルミート多項式が一意・皆無・無限個のいずれの物理的に異なる量子ハミルトニアンを定義するかを係数のみから判定する新しいアルゴリズムが開発され、代数的議論では見えない障壁を明らかにするとともに、有限次元打ち切りが失敗したり誤った力学に静かに収束しうることを示し、単純な非ガウス的ハミルトニアンでも非自明な結果が現れる。

title: Estimation of covariance matrix for Stokes-like measurement under phase-space deformation
abstract: We investigate the signatures of phase-space noncommutativity in an anisotropic oscillator and propose an optomechanical protocol to experimentally characterize it through Stokes-like measurements of an optical field. Starting from a deformed phase-space algebra characterized by the position-position and momentum-momentum noncommutativity parameters $\theta$ and $\eta$, we employ the Darboux transformation to construct an equivalent Hamiltonian in canonical variables. The resulting effective dynamics exhibits correlations between the oscillator degrees of freedom. We derive the corresponding covariance matrix and examine how the noncommutative parameters enter the mechanical dynamics and the optical response. By coupling the oscillator to a coherent optical probe, we obtain analytical expressions for the time-dependent optical coherence attenuation and the nonlinear Kerr phase. We then formulate an interferometric detection scheme through Stokes-like measurements, in which the outgoing optical field is combined with a phase-controlled reference beam at a balanced beam splitter, and the resulting photocurrents are measured using photodetectors. The optical response provides access to the modified normal-mode frequencies, which enables us to estimate experimental values of $\theta$ and $\eta$. Our results establish a theoretical connection between NC-space dynamics, Gaussian-state correlations, and experimentally accessible optical observables, suggesting an optomechanical route toward testing signatures of phase-space noncommutativity.
subjects: Quantum Physics (quant-ph) ; High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th); Mathematical Physics (math-ph)

summaries.en: The paper derives the covariance matrix and Stokes-like optical signatures of an anisotropic oscillator under deformed phase-space algebra with position-position and momentum-momentum noncommutativity parameters theta and eta, proposing an optomechanical interferometric scheme whose coherence attenuation and nonlinear Kerr phase enable experimental estimation of these parameters.
summaries.zh: 本文针对具有位置-位置和动量-动量非对易参数theta与eta的变形相空间代数下的各向异性振子，推导了协方差矩阵及类斯托克斯光学信号，并提出一种光机械干涉测量方案，通过相干衰减与非线性克尔相位来实验估计这两个参数。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、位置-位置および運動量-運動量の非可換パラメータthetaとetaを持つ変形位相空間代数の下での異方性振動子について共分散行列とストークス的測定による光学応答を導出し、コヒーレンス減衰と非線形カー位相を通じてこれらのパラメータを実験的に推定する光機械的干渉測定法を提案する。

title: Resonant Multiphoton Conversion Mediated by a Shared Vibration in Cavity QED
abstract: We show that a vibration shared by two emitter subensembles can jointly establish multiphoton resonance and constructive interference among the virtual exchange pathways responsible for coherent conversion. For opposite displacements with an integer magnitude ratio $r\geq2$, the displacements induced by $r$ excitations in the less displaced subensemble and one in the other cancel exactly, a condition we call displacement neutrality. When the emitter and cavity frequencies match, the resulting composite is resonant with $r+1$ cavity photons, while the vibration-mediated cross interaction makes the conversion pathways add constructively, establishing a direct relation between the displacement ratio and the conversion order. In contrast, independent vibrations can be tuned to the same resonance, but their conversion pathways cancel at leading order, demonstrating that energy resonance alone does not guarantee coherent conversion. For $r=2$, this conversion suppresses three-photon coincidences while leaving the two-photon statistics nearly Poissonian. In the weak-driving limit, interference can also screen the two-photon correlations at all delays from the relative direction of the displacements, whereas the three-photon statistics remain sensitive to it. Because both resonant states leave the vibration undisplaced, their coherence is protected from direct dephasing by the shared vibration, leaving emitter dephasing as the tighter constraint. These results identify relative vibrational displacements as a means of controlling coherent multiphoton conversion and its noise response.

summaries.en: A shared vibration between two emitter subensembles can establish multiphoton resonance and constructive interference among virtual exchange pathways, converting r+1 cavity photons when the displacement ratio is r, while independent vibrations give cancellation at leading order.
summaries.zh: 两个发射体子系综共享的振动可以建立多光子共振并使虚交换路径之间产生相长干涉，当位移比为 r 时实现 r+1 个腔光子的转换，而独立振动则在最低阶发生相消。
summaries.ja: 2つのエミッタ部分集団が共有する振動は多光子共鳴と仮想交換経路間の構成的干渉を確立し、変位比が r のとき r+1 個のキャビティ光子の変換を実現するが、独立した振動では最低次で相殺が生じる。

title: Minimal ancilla for boosting type-I photonic fusion
abstract: Fusion gates enable the creation of large entangled photonic states for linear-optical quantum computing and communication protocols. However, their success probability is limited to $1/2$ without additional photonic resources. Previous schemes for boosting type-I fusion have used four ancillary single photons or a two-qubit Bell state, whose preparation is probabilistic and resource intensive. Here we propose a boosted type-I fusion gate using only two independent ancillary single photons and no entangled ancillary input. It achieves a direct success probability of $5/8$, matching that of the previous four-single-photon proposal while using half as many ancillary photons. The circuit is predominantly passive, with a single active element that applies a phase shift or swaps two modes according to intermediate photodetection outcomes. Unlike the previous schemes, successful outputs occupy fixed modes and require no further conditional output routing. In particular, we show that the gate is more robust to heralded ancillary-photon loss than previously proposed boosted gates and reduces the average number of single photons required to generate a six-qubit ring graph state by more than $4.6\%$ compared with other type-I schemes. It therefore offers a resource-efficient primitive for scalable fusion-based photonic quantum information processing.

summaries.en: A boosted type-I photonic fusion gate using only two independent ancillary single photons and a predominantly passive circuit achieves a 5/8 success probability, matching prior four-single-photon schemes with half the ancilla and greater robustness to heralded photon loss.
summaries.zh: 一种仅使用两个独立辅助单光子和以被动元件为主的电路的增强型I型光子聚变门实现了5/8的成功概率，在辅助光子数减半的情况下达到此前四单光子方案的水平，并对预报辅助光子损耗具有更强鲁棒性。
summaries.ja: 2個の独立した補助単一光子と主に受動的な回路のみを用いる増強型I型フォトニックフュージョンゲートは、先行する4単一光子方式と同等の5/8の成功確率を補助光子半分で達成し、宣言付き補助光子損失に対してより高い頑健性を示す。

title: Neutrinos as Quantum Information Carriers? A Gap Analysis Against the DiVincenzo Criteria
abstract: Photons, trapped ions, neutral atoms, and superconducting circuits are all well-known quantum information platforms. Neutrinos offer a unique possibility, displaying quantum interference (flavour oscillation) over thousands of kilometres, yet interacting so weakly that they can travel through the Earth with minimal interaction. This short paper is a gap analysis. We use information from the existing literature to compare neutrinos to the seven DiVincenzo requirements. Firstly, there are five requirements to do with computation and secondly two requirements to do with communication. We analyse where the gaps are for each requirement. Overall, we find that neutrinos have high fidelity and good coherence; however, they do not have a clear qubit definition and initialisation. They do not have universal gates, individual qubit readout, or stationary-to-flying conversion, meaning they either fail or are very poor. Therefore, we think they are best considered as an exceptional flying information carrier; however, they are very difficult to control. We have outlined all of the gaps which can be used to inform future work.

summaries.en: This gap analysis against the seven DiVincenzo criteria finds that neutrinos offer high fidelity and good coherence as quantum information carriers but lack a clear qubit definition and initialization, universal gates, individual qubit readout, and stationary-to-flying conversion, so they are best regarded as an exceptional but very difficult-to-control flying information carrier.
summaries.zh: 这项针对七项DiVincenzo准则的差距分析发现，中微子作为量子信息载体具有高保真度和良好的相干性，但缺乏明确的量子比特定义与初始化、通用门、单量子比特读出以及静止态到飞行态的转换，因此最好将其视为一种优异但极难控制的飞行信息载体。
summaries.ja: ディビンチェンゾの7つの基準に対するこのギャップ分析は、ニュートリノが量子情報のキャリアとして高い忠実度と良好なコヒーレンスを持つ一方で、明確な量子ビットの定義と初期化、万能ゲート、個別量子ビットの読み出し、静止状態から飛行状態への変換を欠くため、優れているが制御が極めて困難な飛行情報キャリアと見なすのが最適であると結論づけている。

title: Heisenberg-Scaling Quantum Metrology of Electron-Photon Coupling via Multi-Electron PINEM
abstract: Free-electron quantum optics has recently emerged as a promising platform for coherent electron-light interactions, yet its potential for quantum-enhanced metrology remains largely unexplored. Here, we investigate the fundamental precision limit of coupling-strength estimation in multi-electron photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (PINEM), demonstrating that the quantum Fisher information scales quadratically with electron number. We then propose an experimentally accessible scheme combining squeezed-light probing and optical homodyne detection that attains Heisenberg scaling with respect to electron number, provided the electrons exhibit nonzero inter-electron coherence, while surpassing conventional PINEM sensing in photon-number enhancement as well. We further analyze the effect of imperfect electron preparation, showing that electron phase noise is converted into a fluctuating optical displacement and eventually limits the precision. To overcome this limitation, an auxiliary optical mode coupled to the same electron ensemble measures the displacement noise in the signal mode, allowing its conditional suppression and recovery of the Heisenberg scaling. Our work establishes multi-electron coherence as a resource for free-electron quantum metrology and opens the route to precision measurements of nanoscale electron-light interactions.

summaries.en: This paper shows that the quantum Fisher information for coupling-strength estimation in multi-electron PINEM scales quadratically with electron number, and proposes a squeezed-light-plus-homodyne-detection scheme that achieves Heisenberg scaling when electrons have nonzero inter-electron coherence, with an auxiliary optical mode recovering this scaling under electron phase noise.
summaries.zh: 本文表明多电子PINEM中耦合强度估计的量子费舍尔信息随电子数呈二次方标度，并提出一种结合压缩光探测与光学零差检测的方案，在电子具有非零电子间相干性时实现海森堡标度，并通过辅助光学模式在电子相位噪声下恢复该标度。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、多電子PINEMにおける結合強度推定の量子フィッシャー情報が電子数に対して二次でスケールすることを示し、電子間コヒーレンスが非零の場合にスクイーズド光プローブと光学ホモダイン検出を組み合わせてハイゼンベルクスケーリングを達成し、電子位相ノイズ下でも補助光学モードによりこのスケーリングを回復する手法を提案する。

title: From Single Spins to Ensembles: A Calibrated Symbolic Regression Pipeline for NV Spectroscopy
abstract: Characterizing nitrogen-vacancy (NV) ensembles requires connecting their collective spectra to individual centers that experience different local environments. We develop a symbolic-regression pipeline that carries single-center spin structure into a calibrated ensemble model by generating individual spectral responses and combining them with explicit weights. A constrained search selects Hermitian operator terms from single-center optically detected magnetic resonance spectra, fits their coefficients, and retains the selected expressions as source models for the ensemble. Ensemble calibration then accounts for resonance shifts, local disorder, orientation, and optical response while keeping the individual spectral contributions accessible. On public single-center and ensemble data, the zero-field ensemble held-frequency root-mean-square error decreases from 0.008835 to 0.003872 in normalized photoluminescence, a 56.2% improvement over matched uncorrected composition. In controlled QuTiP ensembles of 128 sites spanning four NV orientations, models calibrated at 0 and 3 mT predict an independently held-out 5.17 mT spectrum with errors of 0.000207-0.000228 across three random seeds, comparable to the 0.000200 noise standard deviation. Resolving the simulated response into its individual-center contributions shows how local spectral diversity combines into the ensemble line shape. By retaining the source Hamiltonians while calibrating sample-dependent spectral differences, the pipeline connects local spin physics to collective optical readout and makes the contributions to an ensemble line shape available for physical interpretation.

summaries.en: The paper develops a calibrated symbolic-regression pipeline that derives Hermitian spin-Hamiltonian terms from single NV-center optically detected magnetic resonance spectra and combines them with explicit weights and calibration for shifts, disorder, orientation, and optical response to predict NV ensemble spectra, reducing held-frequency RMSE by 56.
summaries.zh: 该论文开发了一套经过校准的符号回归流程，从单个NV色心的光探测磁共振谱中提取厄米自旋哈密顿量项，并通过显式权重及对共振偏移、局域无序、取向和光学响应的校准将其组合起来预测NV系综光谱，在公开数据上将保持频率的均方根误差降低56.
summaries.ja: 本論文は、単一NV中心の光検出磁気共鳴スペクトルからエルミートなスピンハミルトニアン項を抽出し、明示的な重みと共鳴シフト・局所無秩序・配向・光学応答の較正を組み合わせてNVアンサンブルスペクトルを予測する較正済み記号回帰パイプラインを開発し、公開データで保持周波数のRMSEを56.

title: Quantized-resonance description of a quantum emitter dynamics in a lossy multimode cavity
abstract: In the multimode regime of cavity quantum electrodynamics (cQED), light-matter coupling can be strong enough such as to allows a quantum emitter to couple with multiple resonant field modes. This regime leaves distinctive signatures in the behavior of both the field and the emitter, which are already accessible by modern experimental techniques. To model such effects in lossy cavities, effective discrete-mode approaches have been widely employed, despite their accuracy beyond two modes remaining rarely benchmarked. In this work, we demonstrate the necessity of employing multiple modes to describe the multimode signatures by analyzing the dynamics of an atom in a one-dimensional lossy resonator. The atom's dynamics is simulated using the formalism developed in Weitzel et al. (2026) ( arXiv:2512.18478 ), where a resonance quantization prescription is provided. We investigate its dependency with respect to two different parameters: the light-matter coupling strength and the atom's position. In the former case, we find that the minimal number of modes necessary to capture the essential features of the atom's dynamics increases with the coupling strength. In the latter, we further observe that the multimode regime leads to a strong position-dependency of the atom's dynamics. In all cases, we discuss the physical interpretation of our results and further discuss about how the employed formalism can be used to recover physically relevant quantities.

summaries.en: By simulating an atom in a one-dimensional lossy resonator with a quantized-resonance formalism, the study shows that the minimal number of discrete modes needed to capture the emitter's dynamics increases with light-matter coupling strength and that the multimode regime produces strong position-dependent dynamics.
summaries.zh: 通过采用量子化共振形式体系模拟一维有损谐振腔中的原子，该研究表明，捕捉发射器动力学所需的最少离散模式数随光-物质耦合强度增加而增加，并且多模区域会导致强烈的依赖位置的动力学。
summaries.ja: 量子化共鳴形式を用いて一次元損失共振器中の原子をシミュレーションすることで、本研究は、エミッタの動力学を捉えるのに必要な最小離散モード数が光-物質結合強度とともに増加すること、および多モード領域が強い位置依存の動力学をもたらすことを示した。

title: Spectral fingerprint recognition of mobile signals via Rydberg atomic sensors
abstract: Rydberg-atom sensors have emerged as a promising quantum technology for broadband radio-frequency detection owing to their intrinsic calibration, wide frequency coverage, and high sensitivity. However, their potential for intelligent identification of real-world wireless signals remains largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate a quantum-enabled framework for mobile signal classification based on Rydberg electromagnetically induced transparency spectroscopy and deep learning. Three types of wireless emissions, including cellular voice call, Wi-Fi, and 5G signals from three commercial smartphone brands, are measured to construct a spectral-fingerprint dataset. A convolutional neural network trained on this dataset achieves an initial baseline classification accuracy of 93.44\%. To compensate for spectral drifts induced by temporal and environmental variations, a progressive fine-tuning strategy is employed to continuously adapt the pretrained model, enabling robust classification across diverse deployment scenarios. Furthermore, continuous real-time monitoring is demonstrated under dynamically varying wireless conditions, including cellular voice call, Wi-Fi, and their coexistence. The proposed system achieves an overall frame-level recognition accuracy of 87.67\% over a 60-s measurement. These results establish a pathway toward intelligent quantum radio-frequency sensing and highlight the potential of Rydberg-atom platforms for real-time wireless signal awareness and spectrum monitoring.

summaries.en: Using Rydberg electromagnetically induced transparency spectroscopy combined with a convolutional neural network and progressive fine-tuning, this work classifies mobile signals from smartphones with 93.
summaries.zh: 该工作结合里德堡电磁诱导透明光谱与卷积神经网络及渐进微调策略，对智能手机的蜂窝语音通话、Wi-Fi和5G信号进行分类，基线准确率达93.
summaries.ja: 本研究は、リュードベリ電磁誘導透明分光と畳み込みニューラルネットワークおよび漸進的ファインチューニングを組み合わせ、スマートフォンの携帯音声通話・Wi-Fi・5G信号を分類し、ベースライン精度93.

title: Multimode continuous-variable quantum key distribution with CMOS-compatible photonic-electronic integration
abstract: Multiplexing and photonic-electronic integration offer a route to scalable and high-throughput quantum key distribution (QKD) networks through parallel transmission and compact hardware suited to volume manufacturing. Realizing this route requires multichannel transmitters and receivers, and a security analysis accounting for mode coupling. Here we present a CMOS-compatible photonic-electronic multimode continuous-variable QKD architecture, using polarization multiplexing as a two-mode example. Silicon-photonic transmitter and receiver chips prepare and detect two polarization modes in parallel. The receiver is co-integrated with a dual-channel 28-nm CMOS transimpedance amplifier, providing shot-noise clearances exceeding 20 dB in both channels. Pilot-assisted unitary digital recovery removes the need for active optical polarization control, while a multimode security analysis accounts for the mode crosstalk. At 2 percent residual crosstalk, the multimode analysis extends the simulated secure distance from 39 to 84 km, near the crosstalk-free limit of 89 km. Over 10 km of deployed fibre, the mean total finite-size secret-key rate estimate is 6.69 Mbit/s, 12 percent above the single-mode analysis from the same digitally recovered data. These results establish a route to scalable multimode quantum-secured networks built on technology suited to mass production.

summaries.en: A CMOS-compatible silicon-photonic transmitter and receiver, the latter co-integrated with a dual-channel 28-nm CMOS transimpedance amplifier, enables polarization-multiplexed two-mode continuous-variable QKD in which pilot-assisted digital unitary recovery replaces active polarization control and a multimode security analysis accounting for mode crosstalk extends the simulated secure distance at 2% residual crosstalk from 39 to 84 km, approaching the crosstalk-free limit of 89 km, while achieving a mean finite-size secret-key rate estimate of 6.
summaries.zh: 一种兼容CMOS的硅光发射机与接收机（后者与双通道28纳米CMOS跨阻放大器共集成）实现了偏振复用的双模连续变量量子密钥分发，其中导频辅助的数字化酉恢复取代了主动偏振控制，且计入模式串扰的多模安全性分析在2%残余串扰下将模拟安全距离从39公里提升至84公里、接近89公里的无串扰极限，并在10公里实际部署光纤上获得6.
summaries.ja: CMOS互換のシリコンフォトニクス送信機と、2チャネル28nm CMOSトランスインピーダンスアンプを共集積した受信機により、パイロット支援デジタルユニタリ回復で能動偏光制御を不要にしつつ、モード間クロストークを考慮したマルチモード安全性解析によって2%の残留クロストーク下で模擬安全距離を39kmからクロストークなしの限界89kmに近い84kmへ延伸し、10kmの実敷設ファイバ上で平均有限長秘密鍵率6.

title: Electron-photon entanglement in real space from quantum electrodynamics
abstract: We study the entanglement between an electron and the photon it scatters, resolved in real space and time. Starting from nonrelativistic QED in Fermi's oscillator representation, we write Fock's coupled equations for components with fixed photon number in the photon configuration space, in the length gauge, where the photon is created around the atom through a nonlocal kernel. Truncated at one photon, the equations are solved numerically without the rotating-wave approximation for a one-dimensional model atom in a waveguide with a single transverse mode and enhanced coupling. The atom is driven by a short, off-resonant laser pulse, with the electron and photon represented on real-space grids. The global electron-photon entanglement is largely transient. It peaks during the pulse and decreases as the polarized electron cloud returns to the core, leaving a state close to a product of the electron state and a superposition of the field vacuum with a single scattered photon. Local entanglement, obtained from walkers sampled across both photon-number components, exhibits opposite spatial patterns for the two particles. The electron entropy is smallest at the nucleus and maps the local strength of the dipole coupling, whereas the photon entropy is largest near the atom, where photons are created and absorbed, and smaller in the outgoing wave packets.

summaries.en: Real-space and time-resolved simulations of an electron scattering a photon in a waveguide show that the global electron-photon entanglement is largely transient while local entanglement exhibits opposite spatial patterns for the electron and photon.
summaries.zh: 在波导中对电子散射光子进行的实空间和时间分辨模拟表明，全局的电子-光子纠缠在很大程度上是瞬态的，而局部纠缠在电子和光子上表现出相反的空间分布模式。
summaries.ja: 導波路中で電子が光子を散乱する過程の実空間・時間分解シミュレーションにより、大域的な電子-光子エンタングルメントは主に過渡的である一方、局所的なエンタングルメントは電子と光子で逆の空間パターンを示すことが明らかになった。

title: Parametrically Enhanced Ergotropy and Charging Power in a Three-Mode Bosonic Quantum Battery
abstract: Quantum batteries are quantum systems that potentially serve as fuel for other quantum devices by receiving and supplying energy. In this work, we propose a theoretical scheme to enhance ergotropy and charging power of quantum Battery in the system under consideration through squeezed light. Moreover, The system comprises a coherently driven charger cavity, a strongly dissipative auxiliary cavity acting as a mediator, and an energy--storage battery cavity. Quantum nonreciprocity and directional energy flow are established via destructive quantum interference between the direct coupling path and the loss--engineered indirect path. A degenerate optical parametric amplifier integrated into the charger cavity acts as an active, phase--sensitive energy source that injects two--photon quantum excitations and anomalous correlations. Using a strictly open--quantum--system framework derived directly from the Lindblad master equation, we obtain the full expectation--value dynamics and stationary states. We show that active parametric driving drastically increases the stored energy and peak charging power while maintaining nonreciprocal energy trapping in the battery. We achieve a multi-order-of-magnitude boost in the battery's stored energy, charging power, and ergotropy. We also analyze the effects of pure dephasing on the charging power, ergotropy, and extractable work quality.. Although two--photon pumping introduces photon--number fluctuations that slightly lower the fractional ergotropy ratio ${\cal W}_{\rm B}/{\cal E}_{\rm B}$, the absolute extractable work remains substantially elevated compared to unassisted configurations.
subjects: Quantum Physics (quant-ph) ; Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall); Optics (physics.optics)

summaries.en: The paper theoretically shows that integrating a degenerate optical parametric amplifier into the charger cavity of a three-mode bosonic quantum battery, combined with loss-engineered nonreciprocal energy trapping, boosts stored energy, peak charging power, and ergotropy by multiple orders of magnitude despite a slight reduction in the fractional ergotropy ratio from two-photon-pump-induced photon-number fluctuations.
summaries.zh: 该论文从理论上表明，在三模玻色量子电池的充电腔中集成简并光学参量放大器并结合损耗工程实现的非互易能量囚禁，可使储能、峰值充电功率和遍历功提升多个数量级，尽管双光子泵浦引起的光子数涨落会略微降低遍历功比例。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、三モードボソン量子電池の充電腔に縮退光パラメトリック増幅器を統合し、損失工学による非相反的なエネルギー閉じ込めと組み合わせることで、二光子ポンプ由来の光子数揺らぎによるエルゴトロピー比のわずかな低下にもかかわらず、蓄積エネルギー・ピーク充電電力・エルゴトロピーを複数桁向上できることを理論的に示した。

title: Matching Particle-Arrival Rates for Low-Count Image Denoising
abstract: Low-count imaging arises when limited illumination or dose yields only a few detected particles in microscopy, such as photons or electrons, causing measurements to be dominated by signal-dependent Poisson shot noise. Supervised denoisers typically require paired clean and noisy observations, whereas many self-supervised approaches exploit spatial or temporal redundancy without directly estimating the underlying particle-arrival process. We introduce PARM, a self-supervised denoising framework based on particle-arrival-rate matching. By modeling particle accumulation over exposure as a Poisson counting process, PARM identifies the conditional particle-arrival-rate field with the posterior mean of the latent clean rate. Poisson thinning then splits each observation into complementary lower-exposure views that provide self-supervised rate targets for one another. In implementation, the network estimates the normalized spatial allocation of the conditional rate, while the observed total count determines its global particle mass. Experiments on synthetic data, natural-video sequences corrupted with Poisson noise, and real low-dose electron microscopy demonstrate leading or competitive performance while effectively preserving fine structures. PARM therefore provides a statistically grounded approach to low-count image denoising when clean references are unavailable.
subjects: Image and Video Processing (eess.IV) ; Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (cs.CV)

summaries.en: PARM is a self-supervised denoising framework that models particle accumulation as a Poisson counting process and uses Poisson thinning to create complementary lower-exposure views as rate targets, achieving leading or competitive performance on low-count optical and electron microscopy images without clean references.
summaries.zh: PARM是一个自监督去噪框架，它将粒子累积建模为泊松计数过程，并利用泊松稀疏化生成互补的低曝光视图作为速率目标，在无需干净参考图像的低计数光学与电子显微成像中取得了领先或具有竞争力的性能。
summaries.ja: PARMは粒子の蓄積をポアソン計数過程としてモデル化し、ポアソン間引きを用いて相補的な低露出ビューを率のターゲットとして生成する自己教師ありノイズ除去フレームワークであり、クリーンな参照画像なしで低カウントの光学・電子顕微鏡画像において最先端または競争力のある性能を達成する。

title: Fully-Automated Multi-Modal Registration of Timelapse Zebrafish OCT+LS Images
abstract: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) and light sheet (LS) fluorescence microscopy provide complementary views of tissue morphology and molecular expression, offering a powerful approach for studying embryonic development. However, longitudinal integration of OCT+LS images is challenging because the modalities differ substantially in contrast, spatial resolution, field of view, and visible anatomical features, while embryo growth and movement introduce additional misalignment over time. These challenges stem from both the scale and multimodal nature of the OCT and LS image stacks. We present a fully automated three-dimensional rigid registration framework for aligning OCT and LS volumes of developing zebrafish embryos acquired from 21 to 48 hours post fertilization (HPF). The method does not require pre-existing segmentations or cross-modal feature correspondences, which are often unreliable because OCT and LS capture fundamentally different tissue properties. Registration performance was evaluated across developmental time points using mean target registration error (mTRE) and compared across multiple similarity metrics and optimization methods. Normalized cross-correlation combined with particle swarm optimization produced the most accurate and consistent registration, achieving the lowest mTRE at every evaluated time point compared with the alternative methods. The registration establishes spatial correspondence between OCT tissue morphology and LS fluorescence signals throughout development, enabling integrated longitudinal analysis of structural and molecular changes in living embryos.

summaries.en: This paper presents a fully automated three-dimensional rigid registration framework that aligns OCT and light sheet fluorescence volumes of developing zebrafish embryos from 21 to 48 hours post fertilization without requiring segmentations or cross-modal feature correspondences, with normalized cross-correlation combined with particle swarm optimization achieving the lowest mean target registration error at every evaluated time point.
summaries.zh: 本文提出了一种全自动三维刚性配准框架，用于对齐发育中斑马鱼胚胎（受精后21至48小时）的OCT与光片荧光图像体数据，无需预先分割或跨模态特征对应，其中归一化互相关结合粒子群优化在所有评估时间点均取得最低平均目标配准误差。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、受精後21〜48時間の発生中のゼブラフィッシュ胚のOCTとライトシート蛍光のボリュームを、事前のセグメンテーションやクロスモーダルな特徴対応を必要とせずに位置合わせする全自動三次元剛体レジストレーションフレームワークを提示し、正規化相互相関と粒子群最適化の組み合わせが評価したすべての時点で最小の平均目標レジストレーション誤差を達成した。

title: Extended Target Imaging in Non-Ideal Distributed ISAC Systems: A Hierarchical Off-Grid Approach
abstract: In future integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems, distributed multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) architectures offer high-resolution imaging capabilities. However, reconstructing real-world extended targets is physically challenging due to continuous anisotropic surface scattering and complex occlusions, especially in the presence of system synchronization errors. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a hierarchical two-stage computational imaging framework for extended target reconstruction. In Phase I, an incoherent coarse imaging process is performed to serve as a reliable initializer for subsequent high-resolution coherent image generation. By performing line-of-sight (LOS) interference suppression and leveraging network-wide topological constraints, timing and phase offsets are calibrated. This enables image construction by back-projection (BP) and the coarse identification of target contours using the probabilistic Hough transform (PHT). In Phase II, a joint target position and orientation off-grid compensation model is established, capturing Lambertian diffuse and specular reflections on continuous facets via a first-order Taylor expansion. To tackle severe occlusion and spatial grid mismatches, we propose the bilinear off-grid approximate message passing (BiOG-AMP) algorithm. BiOG-AMP iteratively updates surface visibility and dictionary matrices, enforcing physical consistency across distributed transceiver views. Theoretical analysis derives compressed sensing error bounds, Fisher information limits, and linearization error scaling. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively eliminates imaging artifacts and exhibits superior robustness against synchronization offsets and grid mismatches compared to state-of-the-art baselines.

summaries.en: The paper proposes a hierarchical two-stage computational imaging framework for extended target reconstruction in non-ideal distributed ISAC systems, using incoherent coarse imaging with synchronization calibration in Phase I and a bilinear off-grid approximate message passing algorithm with joint position-orientation off-grid compensation in Phase II.
summaries.zh: 该论文提出了一种用于非理想分布式ISAC系统中扩展目标重建的分层两阶段计算成像框架，第一阶段执行非相干粗成像并校准同步误差，第二阶段采用联合位置与姿态离格补偿的双线性离格近似消息传递算法进行高分辨率相干成像。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、非理想的な分散型ISACシステムにおける拡張目標再構成のため、第1段階で非干渉粗成像と同期誤差校正を行い、第2段階で位置・姿勢のオフグリッド補償を伴う双線形オフグリッド近似メッセージ伝達アルゴリズムを用いる階層型二段階計算イメージングフレームワークを提案する。

title: Dynamic Metasurface-Enabled Generalized Pinching-Antenna Systems
abstract: This article investigates dynamic metasurfaces as an electronic realization of generalized pinching antennas (GPA). By jointly optimizing the locations and radiation coefficients of activated elements, the dynamic metasurface-enabled GPA (DM-GPA) architecture exploits additional design flexibility to enhance spatial reconfigurability beyond that attainable through antenna placement in the conventional pinching-antenna system (PASS). Based on this architecture, we study weighted sum rate (WSR) maximization for multiuser downlink transmission. 1) For two-user transmission, the sum-rate improvement of DM-GPA over conventional PASS is quantified through a lower bound that reveals when the benefit of channel orthogonalization achieved by adjusting the radiation coefficients outweighs the channel power loss caused by the Lorentzian constraint. Furthermore, when conventional PASS yields a rank-deficient channel, DM-GPA is shown to achieve spatial multiplexing and transmit diversity, with a strict sum-rate advantage at sufficiently high signal-to-noise ratios. 2) For general multiuser transmission, a weighted minimum mean-square error (WMMSE)-based alternating optimization algorithm is developed for joint pinching beamforming and digital precoder design. A sequential element-wise search is developed to optimize the locations of the activated elements, with a closed-form solution for the radiation coefficient at each candidate location. Numerical results are provided to demonstrate that: (i) DM-GPA achieves higher WSR than other PASS architectures and fixed-array benchmarks, (ii) increasing the number of activated elements further improves the WSR of DM-GPA, and (iii) radiation coefficient adjustment is particularly beneficial when candidate activation locations are limited.

summaries.en: This paper investigates dynamic metasurfaces as an electronic realization of generalized pinching antennas, where jointly optimizing the locations and radiation coefficients of activated elements yields a DM-GPA architecture with enhanced spatial reconfigurability over conventional pinching-antenna systems, and develops weighted sum rate maximization methods for multiuser downlink transmission.
summaries.zh: 本文研究将动态超表面作为广义夹持天线的电子实现，通过联合优化激活单元的位置与辐射系数，使DM-GPA架构相比传统夹持天线系统具有更强的空间可重构性，并针对多用户下行传输提出了加权和速率最大化方法。
summaries.ja: 本論文では動的メタサーフェスを一般化ピンチングアンテナの電子的実現として検討し、活性化素子の位置と放射係数を同時最適化することで従来のピンチングアンテナシステムを上回る空間再構成性を持つDM-GPAアーキテクチャを構築し、マルチユーザ下りリンク伝送のための重み付き和レート最大化法を開発した。

title: Space-Time Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces for Doppler-Resilient LEO Broadcasting
abstract: Stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIMs) cascade programmable layers in front of a feed. In the SIM designs reported so far, including those proposed for low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites, the layer coefficients are space-only controls or are varied randomly in time to support opportunistic scheduling, so that every radiated beam carries the frequency of the feed. This paper introduces space-time SIMs (ST-SIMs), whose layers are modulated in time and use the temporal dimension of the stack deterministically: each spatial mode of the aperture is paired with its own prescribed frequency translation. The application is LEO broadcasting, where a common waveform reaches terminals with different Doppler shifts, and any common Doppler correction leaves residuals of up to half the Doppler span. We derive the harmonic-domain model of the stack, solve the minimum-energy space-frequency synthesis in closed form, and prove that full column rank of the steering matrix is necessary and sufficient for decoupling K terminal-specific translations, a result that extends to groups of terminals. We further propose a phase-only synthesis algorithm with guaranteed stationarity, together with quantization and control-rate laws. Simulations at 20 GHz over 50 random drops show that a four-layer ST-SIM with a single radio-frequency chain removes the Doppler floor of a static SIM for footprint radii above about 45 km and, under the ideal phase-only model and at equal radiated peak energy, approaches ideal digital per-terminal precompensation within 0.5 dB for resolvable terminals, whereas, in the evaluated geometries, a single time-modulated layer cannot synthesize the required modes.

summaries.en: This paper introduces space-time stacked intelligent metasurfaces that deterministically modulate cascaded layers in time to assign each spatial mode its own prescribed frequency translation, enabling Doppler-resilient LEO broadcasting from a single radio-frequency chain that approaches ideal per-terminal digital precompensation.
summaries.zh: 本文提出了空时堆叠智能超表面，通过确定性地对级联层进行时间调制，为每个空间模式赋予各自预设的频率搬移，从而用单个射频链路实现多普勒韧性低轨广播，其性能接近理想的逐终端数字预补偿。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、積層層を決定論的に時間変調して各空間モードに独自の所定周波数変換を割り当てる時空間積層インテリジェントメタサーフェスを提案し、単一の無線周波数チェーンでドップラ耐性のある低軌道放送を実現して、理想的な端末ごとのデジタル事前補償に近づくことを示す。

title: Analysis and Antenna Position Selection for Pinching-Antenna Systems in Fading Channels
abstract: Pinching-antenna systems (PASSs) are an emerging flexible antenna technology that enables the creation of line-of-sight (LoS) links by repositioning a radiating element along a dielectric waveguide (WG). Most existing studies of PASSs assume a purely LoS environment, despite the fact that many practical wireless environments exhibit scattering and spatially correlated shadow fading. In this paper, we present the first statistical analysis of PASS performance under Ricean fading with spatially correlated large-scale fading. Focusing on a fundamental single-user uplink PASS, we characterize the distribution and mean of the maximum achievable signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). For the classical exponentially correlated shadow fading scenario, we express the channel power process in terms of Brownian motion and derive highly accurate approximations for the maximum SNR distribution and mean. For a general class of smoothly correlated shadow fading processes, we derive an accurate expression for the SNR distribution by modeling the process in terms of the fade sojourn duration. To address the challenges of antenna position selection in fading environments, we propose radio environment map (REM)-based positioning strategies, including opportunistic random-look and grid-based constructions. Analytical results are validated by simulation, and the impacts of key system parameters, such as the Ricean $K$-factor, spatial correlation, WG length, and carrier frequency are investigated. The results provide insights into PASS operation beyond idealized LoS conditions and establish a general analytical framework for performance evaluation and antenna positioning in scattered environments.

summaries.en: This paper provides the first statistical analysis of pinching-antenna systems under Ricean fading with spatially correlated large-scale fading, deriving approximations for the maximum SNR distribution and mean and proposing radio environment map-based antenna positioning strategies validated by simulation.
summaries.zh: 本文首次对存在空间相关大尺度衰落的莱斯衰落信道下的pinching天线系统进行了统计分析，推导了最大信噪比分布与均值的近似表达式，并提出了基于无线电环境地图的天线位置选择策略，且通过仿真验证了理论结果。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、空間相関を有する大規模フェージングを伴うライスフェージング環境下でのピンチングアンテナシステムについて初の統計解析を行い、最大SNRの分布と平均値の近似を導出するとともに、無線環境マップに基づくアンテナ配置戦略を提案し、シミュレーションにより解析結果を検証した。

title: XL MIMO Extreme Learning Machines: Wave-Domain Inference with Stacked Metasurfaces
abstract: The recently envisioned goal-oriented communications paradigm requires machine learning inference to be performed directly on wirelessly transferred data, by splitting neural network computations between the transmitter, the Receiver (RX), and the wireless channel. Such approaches aim to offload large portions of the computation onto the channel itself, which is often controlled by reconfigurable MetaSurfaces (MSs). Typical MS-parametrized systems, however, enable only limited computation offloading in the wave domain, usually corresponding to a single neural network layer, due to adverse channel fading effects and the almost linear operation of the channel and conventional MS models. In this paper, we demonstrate that an eXtremely Large (XL) Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) system equipped with Stacked Intelligent MSs (SIM) at the RX side, together with a single antenna and its accompanying radio-frequency chain, may act as a two-layer neural network operating exclusively over the air. The first (uncontrollable) network layer corresponds to the transformations offered by wireless fading, while the second (controllable) layer is implemented via SIM operations. In particular, only the first, front-end MS layer needs to exhibit nonlinear response to serve as an activation function. Leveraging the Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) framework, the proposed XL MIMO system architecture is shown to be a universal approximator, and the optimal linear-SIM-based combining is derived in closed form, allowing for fast training even and partial signal observability. Numerical evaluations across diverse datasets showcase that the proposed XL-MIMO-ELM framework achieves classification accuracy comparable to idealized digital models, thereby, proving the viability of low complexity, wave-domain neural computations.
subjects: Signal Processing (eess.SP) ; Emerging Technologies (cs.ET); Machine Learning (cs.LG)

summaries.en: An extremely large MIMO system with stacked intelligent metasurfaces at the receiver, combined with an extreme learning machine framework, can perform two-layer neural network inference entirely in the wave domain and act as a universal approximator with classification accuracy comparable to idealized digital models.
summaries.zh: 一种在接收端配备堆叠智能超表面的超大规模MIMO系统结合极限学习机框架，能够完全在波域执行两层神经网络推理，并可作为通用逼近器，其分类精度可与理想化数字模型相媲美。
summaries.ja: 受信側に積層インテリジェントメタサーフェスを備えた超大規模MIMOシステムは、極限学習機械の枠組みと組み合わせることで、波動領域のみで2層ニューラルネットワーク推論を実行でき、理想的なデジタルモデルに匹敵する分類精度を持つ普遍近似器として機能する。
